&

Given, density of water $= 1. 0gmL^{- 1}$
volume of water $= 250mL$

$∴$ Mass of water $=$ density $\times$ volume

$= 1. 0 \times 250 = 250g$

$18g$ of water contains

$= 6. 023 \times {10}^{23}$ molecules

$= \dfrac{6. 023 \times {10}^{23}}{18} \times 250$

questions.q: A closed $10L$ vessel contains $1L$ water gas $\left(1: 1CO: {H}_{2}\right)$ and 9L air~($20 % {O}_{2}$ by volume) at $STP$. The contents of the vessel are ignited. The number of moles of ${CO}_{2},$& in the vessel is closest to :
questions.solution:
Water gas ($CO: {H}_{2}$ is $1: 1$)$= 1$ litre

Air $= 9$ litre

$1$ litre water gas at $STP ⇒ \dfrac{1}{22 . 4}$ moles of gas at $STP$

No. of moles of $CO = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{22 . 4}$ moles

$=$ No. of moles of ${CO}_{2}$ produced after ignition

$= 0 . 022$

questions.q:
The number of moles of water present in a spherical water droplet of radius $1. 0cm$ is,
[Given : Density of water in the droplet $= 10g{cm}^{- 3}$ ]
questions.solution:
Number of moles, $n = \dfrac{mass ( m )}{\text{molar mass} ( M )}$
Given, radius $= 1. 0cm$
$∴$ volume $= \dfrac{4\pi}{3}{cm}^{3}$
Given, density $= 1. 0g{cm}^{- 3}$,

$∴$ Mass $=$ volume $\times$ density $= \dfrac{4\pi}{3}g$
(Atomic weight of water $= 18$ )

$∴ n = \dfrac{4\pi}{3 \times 18} = \dfrac{2\pi}{27}$

questions.q:
An organic compound contains $46. 78 %$ of a halogen $X$. When $2. 00g$ of this compound is heated with fuming ${HNO}_{3}$ in the presence of ${AgNO}_{3}, 2. 21gAgX$
was formed. The halogen $X$ is [Given : atomic weight of $Ag = 108, F = 19, Cl = 355$
$Br = 80, I = 127 ]$
&
questions.solution:
& Mass of $AgX = 2. 21g$
Mass of $X = 46. 78 %$ of $2. 00g$

$= \dfrac{46. 78 \times 2. 00}{100}$

$≅ 0. 94g$
Mass of Ag in AgX must be
$2. 21 - 0. 94g$

$= 1. 27g$
$∴$ Number of moles of $Ag = \dfrac{1. 27}{108}$
which is also equal to number of moles of $X$.
$∴$ Atomic mass of $X = \dfrac{ mass }{' n^{'}}$
$= \dfrac{0. 94 \times 108}{1. 27} ≅ 80$
$∴$ The halogen must be bromine (Br).

questions.q: Natural abundances of ${ }^{12} \mathrm{C}$ and ${ }^{13} \mathrm{C}$ isotopes of carbon are $99 \%$ and $1 \%$, respectively. Assuming they only contributes to the mol. wt. of $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{F}_{4}$, the percentage of $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{F}_{4}$ having a molecular mass of $101$ is
questions.solution:
Percentage of $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{F}_{4}$ of Molar mass $100=\frac{1}{100} \times \frac{1}{100} \times 100=0.01 \%$
Percentage of $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{F}_{4}$ of Molar mass $102=\frac{99}{100} \times \frac{99}{100} \times 100=98.01 \%$
Percentage of $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{F}_{4}$ of Molar mass $101=100-(0.01+98.01)=1.98 \%$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following, the correct statement is :
questions.solution:
There are certain rules for determining the number of significant figures. These are stated below:
(1) All non-zero digits are significant.&
(2) Zeros preceding to first non-zero digit are not significant. Such zero indicates the position of decimal point.
(3) Zeros between two non-zero digits are significant.

(4) Zeros at the end or right of a number are significant provided they are on the right side of the decimal point.&

Hence, 2.005 has four significant figures.
